text:
emily: pushed a tiny config change and CI threw a fit. apparently my laptop is still friends with Windows newlines. :grimacing:

raj: oh no. did the linter summon the ancient newline gods? show the receipts.

emily: here it is:
```
validate-yaml: Error parsing config/deploy.yaml at line 12
  Unexpected carriage return (CR). Expected LF.
  Suggestion: normalize line endings to LF.
```

build-bot: Pipeline failed at stage 'validate-yaml'. Exit code 1. To retry: `ci retry 1773003333`. Logs: https://ci.internal/1773003333 :warning:

kai: classic CRLF strike. also semver drama incoming? sometimes CRLF sneaks into package.json and makes the version string look haunted.

emily: yep, package.json had "version": "1.4.0
" which made deploy-bot do a double-take and refuse to tag it as v1.4.0. deploy-bot: 0 emotions.

morgan: imagine a compiler error that says: "expected ';' but found carriage return. Are we in 1997?" :laughing:

raj: feature idea: a pre-commit hook that normalizes line endings and, on failure, replaces the offending commit message with a randomly chosen compiler meme. morale boost.

kai: even better: require the author to post a GIF of an apologetic penguin in the PR description. penalty and therapy in one. :penguin:

emily: opening PR #704: "normalize-line-endings + pre-commit". description: sorry for the CRLF, here's a penguin GIF.

build-bot: @emily opened PR #704: "normalize-line-endings + pre-commit". Checks queued. :gear:

morgan: bonus meme: "rustc: borrow checker approved. build-bot: CRLF detected. please explain yourself."

raj: adding "CRLF scares deploy-bot" to our watercooler bingo.

emily: thanks team. learned a thing about line endings and the emotional life of bots. closing thread with a tiny victory dance. :dancer:
